contentBlocks.body: Mid-level C# interviews often test whether you can explain how values move through a program. Value types store their data directly, reference types store a reference to an object, and nullable reference types help the compiler flag possible null mistakes before runtime.

Interview signal: do not only say 'classes are reference types.' Explain the failure mode: a null reference crossing a service boundary can become a production exception unless the contract is explicit.

knowledgeItems.prompt: In modern C#, what does `string? GitHubUserName` communicate?

choices: The string is stored on the stack
The property can only be assigned once
The compiler will encrypt the value
The value may intentionally be null
payload.answer: The value may intentionally be null
payload.explanation: Nullable reference type syntax documents that null is allowed and lets the compiler warn when callers forget to handle it.

payload.text: Nullable reference types are a compile-time ____ tool; they do not remove the need for runtime validation at external boundaries.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Which answer best describes why `int CurrentStreak` behaves differently from `LearnerProfile learner`?

choices: `int` is always nullable while classes never are
classes are copied field-by-field on assignment
records are the only reference types in C#
`int` is a value type while `LearnerProfile` is a reference type
payload.answer: `int` is a value type while `LearnerProfile` is a reference type
payload.explanation: Value types contain their data directly; variables of class type hold references to objects.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Implement HandleOrFallback so a missing GitHub handle falls back to the display name.
